title: MCP: serve exact bundled skills as discoverable prompts
body:
## What and why

Refs #480. Bundled modelling and meshing skills are discoverable as stable MCP prompts, with exact source text and a fixed allowlist of three modelling reference resources. Retrieval never executes a modelling command or opens an arbitrary file.

`prompts/list` now treats absent and explicit null cursors identically, matching clients that send `{"cursor": null}`. Non-null cursors and malformed parameters remain errors. Wire regressions cover all three negotiated protocol versions and unchanged, source-identical prompt/resource contents.

This PR stacks the updated modelling skill from #718: parent `04e3c73b01bd28ff1222b3cb68b662d139e78ea4`, followed by one MCP commit. Merge #718 first.

## Validation

Tested source `2dab07c0fbcbe135f640bc8454339b60113ac5d8`, on trunk `3751d3bb93676aa49d1a18c438424be88162ac03`.

- Complete MCP unit suite: 15 passed; workflow integration: 1 passed; no failures/ignores. MCP doc tests: 0.
- Scoped `cargo check`, all-target clippy with `-D warnings`, manual simplification review, formatting and diff checks pass.
- Tests used a cached nine-package `--no-run` build to retain Cargo's dependency-feature resolution; only the emitted MCP normal test binaries executed. The doc-test filter excluded unrelated examples. CPU rendering was forced; no GPU runtime or full workspace gate was run.
- No solver numerics, command schema, result format or oracle case changed.

## Historical demonstration

The original 24-second clip shows prompt retrieval leaving a cantilever unchanged, followed by an explicit tools/call batch running the synthetic conductor recipe. Retrieval and model actions are separate; no desktop prompt selector is implied.

The historical CLI was built at original commit `c515f79e`. Its native host was reused from build `99d8536`, with production source equivalent to branch base `7d9c027d71`; it was not rebuilt at the MCP head. The solver was CPU and the RTX 4090 Vulkan adapter rendered the viewport. The synthetic conduction patch checks an assumed-property calculation, not physical validation or exchanger accuracy. No fresh native capture was made for this cursor correction.

Native GitHub attachments (original capture revision `c515f79ec5856e898154be9e238a139851d8a559`, with the reused viewport/new CLI provenance described above):

- [mcp-skill-prompts.mp4](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4594ef85-25ad-40cd-8292-0d355a16fc11)
- [mcp-model-unchanged.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b34560b-7df0-43f5-8171-87c457050d4e)
- [mcp-connected-conductor.png](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b64c6221-e6b6-4ebf-8cb7-a981fd3ebaff)



## Limits

Clients choose whether to expose prompts and explicitly request model commands afterward. Reference URIs are fixed; other documentation links require the matching checkout. The historical attachments retain their original capture/source provenance. GPU solver support and coupled-exchanger capability are separate release work.

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Thank you, the compile-time allowlist is exactly the right shape, and the traversal tests (`../`, `%2e%2e`, `file:///etc/passwd`, the 100 KB name) are great. This merges right after #718, since it carries the same four skill files.

Nit: `prompts/list` refuses `{"cursor": null}`, which some clients send, so please accept null.

reviews.author: jyviko
reviews.body:
Reviewed. The code is sound: prompt names and resources are a fixed allowlist, path-traversal URIs return -32002, errors are bounded, nothing panics outside tests, and the test that walks `skills/*/SKILL.md` keeps the registry complete.

It's stacked on #718 (04e3c73), so it merges after #718, and it serves #718's broken `docs/lbm-collision.md` link in its prompt text. Once #718 is fixed, please rebase this onto it.
